AccountOut.description: What the backend keeps for an account. Name and email live with the identity provider.
AccountOut.title: AccountOut

AllowanceOut.description: The learner's voice minutes this week, in seconds (spec §6.19).
AllowanceOut.title: AllowanceOut

AnsweredOut.description:
A card answered out loud: what was heard, how close it came, and the rating that points
to. The card is not rated yet.
AnsweredOut.title: AnsweredOut

CallPlanOut.description:
What a practice conversation sets out to practise, as the learner sees it: the kinds of
mistake (a language pack's categories) and the words to use. How the partner is told to
bring them up stays on the server.
CallPlanOut.title: CallPlanOut

CardIn.description:
Which word or correction of a conversation's report to make a card of. The server reads
its content from the report; the app sends none.
CardIn.title: CardIn

CardsAheadOut.description: The cards due within the next days, for the app to review them offline (spec §10.3).
CardsAheadOut.title: CardsAheadOut

CoachEvidenceOut.description:
The facts a suggestion or a finding rests on. Each kind fills the fields it has; the app
words them in the interface language when the model has not.
CoachEvidenceOut.title: CoachEvidenceOut

CoachFindingOut.description: Something that holds the learner back or that went well.
CoachFindingOut.title: CoachFindingOut

CostsOut.description:
A month's estimated spending, for the owner (spec §6.19). Estimates from usage counts and
the configured prices, not the providers' invoices.
CostsOut.title: CostsOut

DataExportOut.description: The learner's copy of their data (6.19): where to read it, for a short time.
DataExportOut.title: DataExportOut

DeviceIn.description: The device and app version a learner chose to send with a message.
DeviceIn.title: DeviceIn

ExamCentreOut.description: The exam centre in one answer.
ExamCentreOut.title: ExamCentreOut

ExamPace.description: How often the week plans a simulation of the learner's speaking test.
ExamPace.title: ExamPace

ExamPhraseBankOut.description: The phrases that help in a speaking test, by function (5.25, spec §6.13).
ExamPhraseBankOut.title: ExamPhraseBankOut

ExamScaleOut.description: How the test reports a result: a band, points out of a maximum, or a level.
ExamScaleOut.title: ExamScaleOut

ExamWeekOut.description: The week's simulations of the learner's speaking test.
ExamWeekOut.title: ExamWeekOut

FlagIn.description:
Reports a partner's line or a correction. The server reads the text from the conversation;
the app sends none.
FlagIn.title: FlagIn

GrammarTopicOut.description:
A topic of the grammar map and how well the learner has it. The app names it in the
interface language.
GrammarTopicOut.title: GrammarTopicOut

HalvesCaseOut.description: A case as one seat sees it (7.4 to 7.9).
HalvesCaseOut.title: HalvesCaseOut

HalvesOut.description:
The hub (7.1): whether Two Halves is open to the learner, their profile, cases, the week's
case, duos, invite and blocks, and the choices of the join form.
HalvesOut.title: HalvesOut

HomeOut.description: The Today screen in one answer.
HomeOut.title: HomeOut

ImportIn.description:
Something to work out: a pasted text, a web page's address, or an uploaded photo. The
field for the `kind` is required, the others are ignored.
ImportIn.title: ImportIn

ImportUploadOut.description: How to send a photo to read: a form POST to `url` with `fields`, then the JPEG as `file`.
ImportUploadOut.title: ImportUploadOut

InboxFeedbackOut.description: A message as the owner reads it. Nobody is named: the owner answers through support.
InboxFeedbackOut.title: InboxFeedbackOut

LevelOutlookOut.description:
`pointing` of the last `counted` conversations point to `next`; the level moves when
`agreeing` of `needed` do.
LevelOutlookOut.title: LevelOutlookOut

LevelStepOut.description: The level the conversation's evidence moved the learner to (spec §6.9).
LevelStepOut.title: LevelStepOut

LookModel.description: A portrait's parts and colors. The app draws exactly these names.
LookModel.title: LookModel

MemoriesOut.description: What the learner's partners know about them, and what the learner set (spec §6.11).
MemoriesOut.title: MemoriesOut

MemoryPatch.description:
What to change about one memory. A key left out is not a change; `day: null` takes an
event's day away.
MemoryPatch.title: MemoryPatch

MemorySettingsPatch.description: A setting left out stays as it is.
MemorySettingsPatch.title: MemorySettingsPatch

MotivationOut.description:
Motivation in one answer: the streak, the next level, the week's quests, the milestones,
moments to celebrate, Monday's recap and a welcome back.
MotivationOut.title: MotivationOut

PenPalReplyOut.description: The learner's voice note, written down, and the partner's answer still on its way.
PenPalReplyOut.title: PenPalReplyOut

PenPalSettingsIn.description: A key left out leaves a setting as it is; the service checks the ranges.
PenPalSettingsIn.title: PenPalSettingsIn

PenPalSettingsOut.description: What the learner chose for their partners' unprompted voice notes (spec §6.16).
PenPalSettingsOut.title: PenPalSettingsOut

Perk.description: What a tier may do beyond talking. Each is checked on the server.
Perk.title: Perk

PersonaDraftOut.description: A persona that is not saved: a template, or one written from a description.
PersonaDraftOut.title: PersonaDraftOut

PersonaIn.description: A new persona. Personality and teaching left out (or null): as their role does.
PersonaIn.title: PersonaIn

PersonaPatch.description:
The parts of a persona to change; the ones left out stay. Personality or teaching set
to null go back to what the persona's role does.
PersonaPatch.title: PersonaPatch

PersonalityModel.description: How a persona comes across. Each trait is a point from 1 to 5 between two poles.
PersonalityModel.title: PersonalityModel

PictureUploadOut.description: How to send a photo: a form POST to `url` with `fields`, then the JPEG as `file`.
PictureUploadOut.title: PictureUploadOut

PlanOut.description: The learner's plan (spec §6.21.2): what they have and what it includes.
PlanOut.title: PlanOut

ProfileChangesOut.description: What a partner changed by voice, newest first (spec §6.1.3).
ProfileChangesOut.title: ProfileChangesOut

ProfileQuestionOut.description: The question about a setting that is due now (spec §6.1.2); null when none is.
ProfileQuestionOut.title: ProfileQuestionOut

ProgressOut.description: The Progress screen in one answer.
ProgressOut.title: ProgressOut

PronunciationAttemptIn.description: A drill said out loud: `target` is the text to say, `drill` how it is practised.
PronunciationAttemptIn.title: PronunciationAttemptIn

PronunciationAttemptOut.description: Recognized words, plus optional provider acoustic scores after explicit consent.
PronunciationAttemptOut.title: PronunciationAttemptOut

PronunciationPickIn.description: Which word of a pair the learner said they heard.
PronunciationPickIn.title: PronunciationPickIn

PushDeviceIn.description:
A phone that may be reached by push (spec §6.18), registered while the learner has
reminders on and the phone allows notifications.
PushDeviceIn.title: PushDeviceIn

QueuedFlagOut.description: A flag as the owner reads it: with the text that was flagged. Nobody is named.
QueuedFlagOut.title: QueuedFlagOut

Reason.description: Why today's part of the plan is what it is.
Reason.title: Reason

RecordingIn.description: A sentence recorded on the device: a correction said again, or a card's answer.
RecordingIn.title: RecordingIn

ReminderNotesOut.description:
What the phone's reminders of the next seven days need besides the week's plan
(spec §6.18): the questions after the learner's events, and a word of the day.
ReminderNotesOut.title: ReminderNotesOut

SceneIn.description: A role-play as the learner reads and edits it, in their explanation language.
SceneIn.title: SceneIn

SoundScoreOut.description: How a drill's sound went, from the acoustic provider's phoneme scores (0-100).
SoundScoreOut.title: SoundScoreOut

SoundSummaryOut.description: A problem sound of the language being learned, with what the learner did on it.
SoundSummaryOut.title: SoundSummaryOut

SpeakingExamOut.description: A speaking test the exam centre simulates (spec §6.13).
SpeakingExamOut.title: SpeakingExamOut

StoryIn.description:
Who tells the next episode: one or two of the learner's partners; empty for the series'
own cast.
StoryIn.title: StoryIn

StorySummaryOut.description: An episode in the series' list, without its lines.
StorySummaryOut.title: StorySummaryOut

TeachingModel.description:
How a persona treats mistakes and adapts to the learner. Every key is always present;
null means "as the learner's profile says" (or, for speed, the voice's own pace).
TeachingModel.title: TeachingModel

WeekPlanOut.description: This week's plan (the Learning Director, spec §6.12), as it stands now.
WeekPlanOut.title: WeekPlanOut

WeekReviewOut.description:
Last week's check-in (spec §6.12): its numbers, and a few sentences from the partner
once they are written.
WeekReviewOut.title: WeekReviewOut

WordDetailsOut.description: A word's forms (spec §6.7); a form the word does not have is null.
WordDetailsOut.title: WordDetailsOut

post.description: Writes a copy of everything kept for the learner and says where to read it.

Makes a flashcard of a word or a correction in a conversation's report. Saving one
that is a card already answers with that card.

get.description: The cards due within the next days, so the app can review them offline.

post.description:
Stores ratings the app gave, perhaps offline, in the order they were given. Sending
the same batch again stores nothing twice; the server's card wins over an older rating.

get.description: One of the learner's cards (a word of the day opens it).

post.description:
Hears a card answered out loud (voice review) and says how close it came. The card
is rated as before, by the learner.

get.description:
Where the card's sound plays from: the word with its sentence, or a correction as it
is right, in the learner's partner's voice. Made the first time it is asked for.

Today's suggestions from the Coach, with what holds the learner back, what went well
and earlier suggestions (5.1, 5.26).

post.description: The learner's answer: do it, not now, or not for me (with why).

get.description: What the learner reported in a conversation.

put.description:
Reports a partner's line or a correction (spec §16.1). Reporting one again changes the
reason and puts it back in the owner's queue.

post.description: Says correction `index` of a conversation's report again ("Say it better").

get.description: The corrections of a conversation's report the learner said again.

post.description:
Asks for a report that is not there: for an earlier conversation, or again after one
failed. Answers at once; the report is written in the background.

get.description: Where a part's model answer plays from, in the examiner's voice.

post.description: Asks again for a score that could not be written.

get.description: The cards of the learner's next simulation of a speaking test, to prepare with.
The phrases that help in a speaking test, by what they do (5.25).

post.description: Sends the owner a bug report, an idea or any other message (spec §6.21.4).

get.description: Every grammar topic of the language learned, with how well the learner has it.
One topic of the map, with the learner's own mistakes on it.
The Two Halves hub (7.1).

post.description: A case against an AI stand-in (7.3).
Records a move (7.6): written down at once, checked before the other hears it.
A code to play with a friend (7.12).
Acts on a clue heard (7.7): an option of the board's question.
Reports a move heard (7.10): hidden at once, and queued for the owner.

delete.description: Deletes the learner's Two Halves data and withdraws the voice-sharing consent (7.11).

put.description: Joins Two Halves, or changes the join answers (7.2).

get.description: The owner's Two Halves queue (6.15): held moves and reports.
What the learner brought, for the language they are learning, newest first (§6.17).

post.description: Works out a pasted text, a web page or an uploaded photo at the learner's level.
A form for one photo (a JPEG) to read: a menu, a letter, an article, a book page.

Makes a flashcard of one of an import's words. One that is a card already answers
with it.

get.description: What the learner's partners know about them from earlier conversations.

patch.description: Turns memory on or off, or names the topics partners leave alone.

post.description:
Takes back a "forget that" said during the call that is still going on: what it hid
is remembered again. Once the call has ended it is final.

get.description:
The streak, the next level, the week's quests, the milestones and the moments to
celebrate (spec §6.15).

post.description: The app showed a moment: it is not shown again.

put.description: Pauses the reminders and the quiet-week nudge (`days`), or resumes them (null).

get.description: The learner's own role-plays in the language they learn now, the latest first.

post.description: Keeps a role-play the learner wrote or had written.
A role-play written from a situation the learner described; kept only once saved.
What a situation described out loud says, to edit before a scene is written.

get.description: A month's estimated spending (this month unless `month` names its first day).
The owner's inbox of feedback (open messages unless `status` says otherwise).

put.description: Marks a message done, or open again.

get.description: The owner's review queue (open flags unless `status` says otherwise).

put.description: Closes a flag as resolved or dismissed, or opens it again.

get.description: The learner's pen-pal settings and a line per partner (spec §6.16).

post.description: Has a note or an answer that failed written again (three attempts in all).

put.description: Turns the partners' unprompted voice notes on or off, and sets how often and when.

get.description: One partner's thread: every note, oldest first, with an address to play each.

post.description:
Asks a partner for a voice note now. It is written in the background: the note is
pending until the thread shows it ready.
The learner opened a thread: what the partner sent is read.

Answers a partner with a voice note: written down at once, word for word; the
partner's answer follows in the background.

get.description: The learner's phrases for the language they are learning, newest first (spec §6.7).

post.description: Keeps a phrase in the phrasebook. Keeping one that is kept already answers with it.
Phrases for a situation the learner describes, nothing kept until they choose.
Makes a flashcard of a kept phrase. One that is a card already answers with it.

get.description: What the learner has bought and what it includes (spec §6.21.2).
What a partner changed by voice, newest first (spec §6.1.3).

post.description: Puts a setting back to what it was before a change made by voice.

get.description: The question about a setting that is due now, if one is (spec §6.1.2).

post.description: Applies the learner's answer to a question about a setting.
The learner does not want to answer now: the question comes back once, later.
Hears a drill said out loud and says, word by word, what was heard as asked.

get.description:
Where a word or sentence of the lab plays from, in the learner's partner's voice. Only
the lab's own texts and the learner's problem words can be asked for.

post.description: Remembers which word of a pair the learner heard; right if it was the one played.

get.description:
The problem sounds of the language the learner learns, with their practice so far
(spec §6.14). Empty for a language that has none yet.
The words the learner was asked to say and missed, not yet said right twice in a row.

put.description: Lets the server reach this phone: reports, scores and a nudge after a quiet week.

delete.description: This phone is not to be reached any more (reminders off, signing out).

get.description:
Events of the learner's life to rehearse before they happen and to talk over after;
`local_date` is today on their device.

post.description: The role-play that rehearses an event, written the first time it is asked for.

get.description: Whether the audio of the learner's conversations is kept (spec §6.6).

patch.description: Keeps recordings, or stops: stopping deletes every recording kept so far.

get.description: The learner's listening series (5.29): its episodes, the newest first.

post.description:
Asks for the next episode, told by one or two partners. It is written in the
background: the episode is pending until it is ready.

get.description: One episode, with an address to play each line.

post.description: A question about the episode answered out loud, written down and checked.
The learner listened to the end: the episode's words count as heard.

get.description:
What the conversations of the last `days` days (7, 30 or 90) showed, for the
learner's own teacher (6.23).
Two recorded conversations of the same kind, weeks apart, to hear side by side.

post.description: Asks the Tutor about one correction of a conversation's report (spec §6.5).

get.description: The questions the learner asked the Tutor, newest first.

post.description: Asks the Tutor a question about the language learned (spec §6.8).

get.description: Last week's check-in, to follow one being written; `week` is its Monday.

post.description: Has last week's check-in written (once); `week` is its Monday.

get.description: Where the check-in plays from, spoken by the partner who wrote it.
